chunks: His father, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil, Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Natanat, al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mo'adab, and Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamedany - may the Sublime God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sani (peace be upon him) that he heard him say:
God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand words. Each word opened up to one thousand new words.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ال: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sani (the second Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'one thousand words' taught to Imam Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq narrates that the Prophet Muhammad taught Imam Ali (peace be upon him) 'one thousand words,' each serving as a key that unlocks a thousand more, illustrating the concept of *al-kalimat al-ma'tumun* (the entrusted words). This hierarchical model of knowledge underscores the Imam's role as the comprehensive interpreter of divine revelation, bridging the exoteric and esoteric dimensions of the Quran. The narration reflects the Shia belief in the Imam's unique capacity to derive infinite legal and spiritual insights from concise divine utterances.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-36 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil, Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih, Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, Hamzih ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Natanat, al-Hussein ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mo’adab and Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamedany - may the Sublime God be pleased with them - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted hi father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih that had heard Abi Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sani (MGB) say, “
God’s Prophet (MGB) taught Ali (MGB) one-thousand words. Each word opened up to one-thousand new words.”
